To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a bridge functional that imposes the correct second order derivative of the free energy density with respect to the density and the correct pressure is able to correct the solvation free energy and structure of hydrophobic nanoclusters in water, and (2) this functional can be obtained from an expansion around the bulk liquid state.

the bridge functional that correct to all orders the thermodynamic inconsistency of the homogenous reference system in the common approximation to the integral equation theory for water is given by the sum of a third order expansion around the liquid density and a metastable gas reference system, and that this theory predicts the solvation of hydrocarbons and hard sphere solvates in water at room conditions in quantitative agreement with molecular dynamics simulations.

the thermodynamic inconsistency of the common hyperneted chain approximation to the liquid-gas interface is corrected by a bridge functional that imposes the correct pressure and second order derivatives, and that the resulting theory is quantitatively correct for hydrophobic solubility and solvation free energy.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a molecular density functional theory for liquid water that has liquid-gas coexistance and correct pressure and that can be used for the study of hydrophobic hydration of large solutes.
the development of a theory for the solvation of hydrocarbons in water at room conditions.
the thermodynamics of the liquid-gas co-existence of water.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new theory gives the best description of water and its hydrophobic hydration so far.
the theory presented here provides a new and promising approach to study the solvation of hydrocarbons in water.
the theory presented here is a major improvement of the theory of hydrophobic hydration.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the theory is now able to predict all thermodynamic properties of water and hydrophobic solvations with quantitative accuracy.
molecular density functional theory with a bridge functional can now be used for hydrophobic hydration and solvation of large hydrophobic solute molecules.
the bridge function is not just a mathematical trick but a physical model of the liquid-gas interface.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a correct description of liquid-gas co-existence is essential for an accurate molecular theory of hydrophobic hydration.
the thermodynamic consistency of molecular density functional theories is important for the correct description of hydrophobic hydration.
the thermodynamic properties of liquid water are not well described by the hypernetted chain equation of state.
